svg.title: Physical storage and address microscope — input_preprocess_window_downsample_c32_fp16
svg.desc: Physical allocations, exact byte counts, a worked producer/consumer address, lane words, and bank mapping specialized to this kernel. Native panel bank rows show address regions rather than hardware transaction cycles.
svg.text: 1 warps · Half operand elements (2 B) · 2,048 explicitly declared shared bytes
CTA-local storage actually used by this entry
Feature stores → block barrier → Half adapter gathers A words. C32 body stays in registers.
Follow one address into lane 13 — bases and address spaces stay separate
Feature pixel (3,0), plane 0: s_Plane[0][3] begins at shared byte 48.
Adapter lane 13, word 0 selects pixel 3 and uint32 component 1 → shared byte 52.
This Half word contains feature channels 2 and 3. Adapter K=16; its output has C32.
Feature storage is row-major by pixel, unlike the later native MMA packet layout.
Labels are panel-relative; add the model channel base. This is an operand fragment, not a contiguous token vector.
Address bits, banks, and the next consumer
Pixel 3, component 1 → byte 52 → bank 13. Do not reuse
The adapter’s word gather performs the layout conversion from pixel-major features to MMA A registers.
Next consumer: full C32 skip + pooled C32
Shared reuse requires the source barrier sequence; register publication can stay inside the current warp.
The source determines cache policy. No cache residency, issue-cycle schedule, spill count or speedup is assumed.
